Interpreting the fractions as division, we get

$$
(12\,{\color{red}{\div\, 7}})\times(21\,{\color{blue}{\div\, 4}}).
$$

 

Since our expression contains multiplication and division only, we can create an equivalent expression by swapping the ${\color{red}{\div\, 7}}$ and ${\color{blue}{\div\, 4}}$:

$$
(12\,{\color{blue}{\div\, 4}})\times(21\,{\color{red}{\div\, 7}})
$$

 

Interpreting the divisions as fractions, we get

$$
\dfrac{12}{4}\times\dfrac{21}{7}.
$$

Carrying out the divisions, we arrive at

$$
\begin{aligned}{{\frac{12}{4}}_{⏟}}_{3}\times {{\frac{21}{7}}_{⏟}}_{3}=3\times 3=9.\end{aligned}
$$
